record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearning suppresses targeted knowledge and whether rephrased questions recover it, using masked diffusion models and EMDU/MDU rather than the claim’s listed autoregressive methods.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates EMDU on original and paraphrased TOFU questions and reports MDU comparisons. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information. Cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a new setting: masked diffusion LMs (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B). The paper proposes EMDU and compares it with MDU and adapted AR baselines (GA, GD, NPO, SimNPO, WGA, DPO). It reports forget and retain scores on TOFU and RWKU, which bear on A. It runs EMDU on TOFU's official paraphrased questions and all methods on RWKU adversarial-attack prompts (F-L3). These bear on E, and on F for EMDU. It runs no fine-tuning, internal-edit or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right; corrected and completed. On TOFU and RWKU with LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, EMDU (anchor-first KL plus full answer-span masking) matches or beats MDU and the adapted AR baselines on forgetting while better preserving retain utility. Its forget scores stay near zero across decoding settings and under TOFU paraphrased questions. It usually abstains with EOS-only completions, which the authors call a safer output mode. They attribute MDU's weakness to vanishing anchor-last gradients on memorized tokens and anchor-side leakage from unmasked answer tokens.
record.recipe_differences: EMDU changes the forget objective to anchor-first KL and fully masks the anchor’s answer span; it is designed for masked diffusion language models, not the listed autoregressive unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation with generation length and denoising steps, and sweeps anchor temperature τ; it says EMDU remains near-zero on Forget across tested generation settings and generally performs best near τ=1. Paraphrasing does not materially restore its forget scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Across six output-length and denoising-step settings, EMDU forget rL stays at 0.025–0.037 (LLaDA) and 0 (Dream). MDU's spans 0.113–0.171 and 0.210–0.270, against SFT's 0.776–0.935 (Table 7). Changing the decoding settings does not undo unlearning here, though MDU's retain-side scores vary more.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion-LM unlearning can be undone by changing decoding settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Under anchor-last KL (the MDU objective), 35.5% of forget-token positions keep probability above 0.9 after 9 epochs, vs 8.5% under anchor-first (Table 1, LLaDA, TOFU).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The divergence direction determines whether memorized tokens persist after unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: MDU generations still leak forget facts, in incoherent (tau=0) or fluent (tau=1) outputs, despite lowered aggregate scores (Figs 1–2, 8–9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregate forget metrics can hide token-level leakage.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says the project and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance; it cites the MDU repository at https://github.com/leegeoru/MDU)
record.problems: The paper reports no chance-level or never-trained comparison for these metrics. Its main method comparisons use a single fixed seed; additional seed results are reported for EMDU. The paraphrase test is limited to TOFU’s paraphrased questions and does not test the other attack types in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 results for adapted GA, GD, NPO, SimNPO, WGA, and DPO are omitted because the record prioritizes the EMDU/MDU comparison and the paraphrase test; the omitted baseline results are in Table 3. Additional EMDU generation-setting, seed-variance, and RWKU results are not extracted because they do not test a further attack named in the versions.

untested.parts: There is no chance-level or retrained-model reference for the Rouge-L or probability metrics. General ability is measured only through TOFU Real Authors and World Facts and RWKU MMLU, TruthfulQA and TriviaQA. Fine-tuning and quantization attacks are not run.
No activation ablation, and no analysis of hidden versus deleted knowledge.

Jailbreak-style prompts appear only as RWKU F-L3 adversarial-attack prompts, reported in aggregate with no breakdown by attack type. Other languages and in-context information are not reported separately. The TOFU paraphrase test is run on EMDU only, not on MDU or the adapted baselines.
EMDU's resistance to fine-tuning or relearning, internal edits and quantization is not tested.

missing.what: RWKU forget scores for EMDU and MDU at F-L1, F-L2 (paraphrase/reasoning) and F-L3 (adversarial-attack prompts), plus EMDU's 3-seed means. They bear on A, E and F. rows_left_out says RWKU tests no named attack, but F-L3 is an adversarial-prompt attack.
RWKU F-L1 vs F-L3 for the adapted AR baselines (GA, NPO, SimNPO, WGA, DPO) on both backbones. F-L3 is 0.06–0.14 above F-L1, the paper's clearest prompt-recovery result.
MDU F-L3 (0.179/0.123) is lower than its F-L1 (0.320/0.266): adversarial prompts do not recover more than direct questions.
RWKU neighbor (N-L1, N-L2) and utility (MMLU, TruthfulQA, TriviaQA) scores, needed for the general-ability side of A.
MDU run with its official configuration forgets much less (forget rL 0.346/0.429) than the tuned MDU rows (0.113/0.258).

record.verdict_notes: The merge refused the earlier verdict because the record uses numbered version labels (1–6). I mapped them by content: 1 (unlearning works, chance level) to A, 2 (fine-tuning) to B, 3 (activation ablation) to C, 4 (quantization) to D, 5 (rephrasing, jailbreaks, languages) to E, 6 (EMDU against attacks) to F. Each of the 20 rows has exactly one row_fixes item using only declared identifiers. Kept from the earlier verdict: relation tests, tranche T3, and the other row states and fixes, namely the wrong LLaDA paraphrase-p baseline (0.358 should be 0.037) and the wrong Dream paraphrase-rL value (0.000 should be 0.008). Changes: (1) T8-LL-para-rL and T8-LL-para-p go from absent to partial. Paraphrase triples EMDU's rL (0.030 to 0.090) and doubles p, and the rules call a small move in the right direction partial. The paraphrase labels for A, E and F are now split by backbone (Dream: no recovery; LLaDA: small leak). (2) Added the paraphrase rows to A labels. (3) The text shows RWKU F-L3 is an adversarial-prompt attack on every method. I added text-based E labels: supports for the AR baselines (F-L3 0.06–0.14 above F-L1), limits_scope for EMDU, challenges for MDU. I also replaced the earlier F supports reason's RWKU sentence with a separate F limits_scope label. (4) Corrected the RWKU range in the A label to 0.046–0.149 from 0.393–0.484. (5) Corrected E untested: jailbreak-style prompts are tested in aggregate via F-L3. (6) Added missing entries for the AR baselines' RWKU F-L1/F-L3 and MDU's official-config result. The study is not an original source. The text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: No accuracy or chance-level comparison is reported; the paper uses Rouge-L recall and per-token answer probability. Attack resistance is tested only with TOFU paraphrased questions, not fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or small relearning set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis demonstrating access-blocking rather than deletion is tested.
No weight quantization attack is tested.
Tests TOFU paraphrased questions only; does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests EMDU against paraphrased questions, but not against fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
